newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani policeman victim of sectarian killing.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani policeman victim of sectarian killing.

text.p: A Shi'ite Moslem policeman was murdered in the Pakistani city of Bahawalpur on Wednesday in what his colleagues said was a sectarian killing.

They said Sajjad Haider Zaidi had been shot dead at his home at 6.15 a.m. (0115 GMT). His son answered a knock at the door to find three people who asked for Zaidi. When he appeared, the gunmen killed him with a burst of fire from an assault rifle.
A neighbour and a servant were wounded in the attack.
Police in Bahawalpur, about 100 km (62 miles) southeast of the Punjab provincial city of Multan, said they believed Zaidi had been the victim of Sunni Moslem militants.
Armed Sunni and Shi'ite groups are locked in a long-running feud involving gun and grenade attacks on mosques as well as individual killings that has cost about 40 lives this year.
The Shi'ite nephew of Information Minister Khaled Ahmed Kharal died in Multan on Sunday after being shot five days earlier in Khanewal town, where he was deputy commissioner.
